concerns: Sealed-holdout reuse: walk-forward replay over sealed_holdouts.jsonl erodes seal integrity; any window already consumed by a prior reject/promote decision cannot serve as independent evidence for a later one
Multiple-testing inflation: repeated rechecks of rejected candidates degrade effective significance with no stated correction (no deflated-Sharpe / White reality check / familywise-error control)

Zero supporting evidence in the proposal: current_evidence shows PF=None, EV=None and the decay-fraction claim ('meaningful fraction') is unquantified — the hypothesis should be measured from outcome logs BEFORE the gate is modified

Gate-weakening risk: a decay-aware recheck is semantically a looser rejection criterion; champion promotion must remain exclusively via research_promote_champion.py / promote.py with all gates passing, and a flipped decision must carry registry lineage to the original rejection

Lookahead exposure: replay must be point-in-time strict (replay clock, features computed only from data available at each replay timestamp); nothing in the proposal states how this is enforced or tested
Cost fidelity unspecified: outcomes must be net of the runner's actual spread/slippage assumptions per AGENTS.md rule 6; the replay cost model is not defined
Scope ambiguity in bot/intel/: proposal must confirm runtime intel components remain read-only with respect to broker positions and gain no order capability
Falsification criterion covers exploration trades but not the offline phase; there is no stated kill-condition for the replay itself
votes.reason: The core hypothesis (short-horizon edge decay masquerading as gate rejection) is plausible and worth testing, and the proposed mechanism is offline-only over existing records with no execution-path or config impact, so no safety violation is apparent. However, as written the design has two methodological defects that would corrupt gate integrity if shipped: (1) rolling revalidation replayed against the same sealed_holdouts.jsonl records converts the sealed holdout into a reusable selection dataset, which is textbook holdout erosion — repeated looks inflate false-positive promotions; and (2) 'PF=None, EV=None' means no evidence exists yet that decay-driven rejections are a meaningful fraction at all. The change also functionally weakens the validated-state gate (a second look that flips rejections to acceptances), so it must be framed and implemented as generating a NEW challenger evaluation through the governed promote path, not as a direct state flip.
requested_revisions: Phase 0 measurement study: quantify from ExperimentRegistry/outcome logs what fraction of gate rejections exhibit decay-vs-absent-edge profiles; report the number and only proceed if it clears a pre-stated minimum fraction

Holdout hygiene rule: revalidation may only score windows never previously consumed by any decision for that candidate; fitting uses pre-window data, scoring uses untouched post-rejection data; document per-candidate window consumption in the registry
Multiple-testing control: apply an explicit correction (e.g., deflated Sharpe, White's reality check, or Bonferroni-style alpha adjustment across repeated looks) and state the adjusted threshold

Governance framing: revalidation output may only mint a new challenger evaluation through the standard promote path; validated-state can never be flipped in place; every replay recorded in ExperimentRegistry with lineage to the original rejection experiment id
Point-in-time enforcement: implement a replay-clock guard plus a dedicated leakage regression test proving features never access post-timestamp label data
Specify the exact net-of-cost model (spread/slippage matching the runner config) used inside the replay and require costed expectancy in all reported metrics
Concrete test plan: unit tests for horizon alignment arithmetic, leakage regression test, registry-integration test, and a test that a failing replay leaves validated state untouched
Add an offline-phase falsification criterion: e.g., abandon the approach if revalidated candidates show no statistically significant net-of-cost expectancy uplift on untouched windows
Explicit statement that all bot/intel/ and bot/ai_council/ changes preserve read-only research constraints (no mt5.order_send() reachable from any touched code path)

concerns: Candidate-specific horizon selection can introduce selection bias or lookahead.
The proposed gate change may weaken validated-state requirements without predefined acceptance thresholds.
PF/EV are currently absent, so expected benefit is unsubstantiated.
Falsification based on exploration trades conflicts with the stated strictly offline replay scope.
votes.reason: Offline, costed rolling walk-forward revalidation is compatible with research-only governance, but the proposal lacks a precise leakage-safe protocol and promotion safeguards.
requested_revisions: Specify horizon selection, rolling folds, embargo/purge rules, minimum sample sizes, and net-cost metrics before evaluation.
Pre-register fixed pass/fail thresholds versus the current static gate using sealed holdouts only.
Require no champion promotion unless existing governed promotion gates also pass unchanged.
Replace exploration-trade falsification with offline OOS falsification criteria; keep any DEMO observation separate and read-only for research components.
Add tests proving no future records, outcome labels, or post-window registry data enter each fold.

votes.reason: The proposal is plausibly safe as an offline research experiment, but evidence, scope, and safeguards are insufficiently specified. A rolling walk-forward gate could affect candidate promotion or downstream DEMO exploration unless isolation and governance are explicit.
requested_revisions: Specify exact files, functions, and an offline-only execution path with no MT5 order capability.
Define candidate horizon alignment, rolling-window parameters, minimum sample sizes, costs, and no-lookahead rules.
Provide baseline versus revised gate metrics and predefine quantitative promotion/rejection thresholds with uncertainty reporting.
Require ExperimentRegistry registration and immutable input snapshots for every replay.
Add an explicit hard gate preventing champion writes and runtime deployment until separately approved by the governed promotion process.
Clarify that the experiment produces no exploration trades; if trades are later enabled, submit a separate proposal with risk and execution controls.
Define a tested rollback procedure and run the required lifecycle and OOS validation tests with before/after pass counts.
